title: Process Matters more than Output for Distinguishing Humans from Machines
abstract: arXiv:2605.06524v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Reliable human-machine discrimination is becoming increasingly important as Large Language Models and autonomous agents are deployed in online settings. Existing approaches evaluate whether a system can produce responses indistinguishable from those of a human. This approach follows the focus on the output of a machine, as suggested by Alan Turing. Cognitive science provides an alternative approach: considering the process by which that behavior is produced. To evaluate whether processes can reliably distinguish humans from machines, we introduce a process-based framework, the Process Turing Test, and evaluate it across a battery of cognitive tasks spanning decision-making, working memory, and planning. These tasks, such as mental rotation and sequence prediction, yield process-level measures complementing conventional measures of overall task performance. translated_title: 在区分人类与机器时，过程比输出更重要
translated_abstract: 随着大语言模型和自主智能体被部署到在线环境中，可靠的人机判别正变得日益重要。现有方法评估的是系统能否产生与人类无法区分的回答，这一思路遵循了图灵所倡导的关注机器输出的理念。认知科学提供了一种替代思路：考察产生该行为的过程。为了评估过程能否可靠地区分人类与机器，我们提出了一个基于过程的框架——过程图灵测试，并在一系列涵盖决策、工作记忆和规划的认知任务上对其进行评估。这些任务（如心理旋转和序列预测）能够提供过程层面的测量指标，以补充传统的整体任务表现测量。我们还在测试组合中纳入了多种验证码（CAPTCHA）任务。在整个测试组合中，过程……
tldr: 该论文提出“过程图灵测试”框架，证明通过考察行为产生的过程（而非仅看输出结果）能够更可靠地区分人类与机器。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the Process Turing Test, showing that analyzing the processes by which behavior is produced on cognitive tasks distinguishes humans from machines more reliably than evaluating outputs alone.
